items.plain: Does knowing all these things please You, God of truth? Unhappy is one who knows them all but not You; happy is one who knows You without them. One who knows both is happier only because of You, if he glorifies You, is thankful and not vain.

From You I had learned that words are not true because eloquent, nor false because clumsy. Wisdom and folly are like healthy and unhealthy food, and fine or plain words like fancy or simple dishes: either food can be served in either dish.

I lied to my mother and slipped away while she spent the night near Cyprian's chapel, and You forgave me. Her daily tears begged You, Lord, to stop me sailing; but You, hearing her deeper wish, refused that request to make me what she always prayed for.

I told myself some other nature in me sinned, not I; it pleased my pride to escape blame. But it was wholly me, divided against myself. Worst of all, I would rather have You, Almighty God, defeated in me to my ruin than be overcome by You and saved.
I chased honours, money and marriage, and You laughed at me. In those desires I suffered bitterly, and You were kinder the less You let anything that was not You become sweet to me.

My sins multiplied. The woman I lived with was sent back to Africa, vowing to You never to know another man, and my heart bled. No lover of marriage but a slave to lust, I took another, and the wound did not heal: the pain dulled but grew more hopeless.

How crooked my paths! Woe to the soul that hoped to gain something better by leaving You. It tossed every way and found only pain; You alone are rest. Yet You are near, rescue us from our wanderings, set us on Your way and promise to carry us through.
Prompted to return to myself, I went into my inmost self with You as my Guide and Helper. With my soul's eye, such as it was, I saw above my mind the Unchangeable Light.
After You had quietly soothed my head and closed my eyes to empty things, my old frenzy calmed. I awoke in You and saw You infinite, in a way that did not come through the senses.

I marvelled that I now loved You, and not some fantasy in Your place. Yet I did not hold on to You: Your beauty lifted me up to You, and my own weight, the habit of the flesh, soon dragged me back down in sorrow.

I was now certain of Your eternal life, though I saw it dimly, and no longer doubted an incorruptible source of all things. I wanted not more certainty about You but more steadiness in You. Yet my daily life still wavered, and my heart needed cleansing of the old ways.
Woe is me! How high You are in the heights and how deep in the depths! You never leave, yet we hardly ever return to You.

The world held me down pleasantly, as in sleep; my thoughts of You were like someone half waking and sinking back. I knew giving myself to Your love was far better than giving in to my desires, but the one convinced me while the other pleased me and held me.

When You showed me on every side that Your words were true, I had no answer but sleepy words: soon, in a little while. That soon never came. I delighted in Your law inwardly, but another law in my body fought my mind and held me captive to sin.

While Pontitianus spoke, You, Lord, turned me to face the self I had hidden behind my back, and I saw how foul I was. I could not flee; You kept setting me before my eyes to see my sin and hate it, though I had pretended not to see it.
Wretched as I was, in early youth I had begged You for chastity, saying: give it to me, but not yet. I feared You would answer quickly and cure a desire I wanted satisfied, not ended.

I condemned and lashed my soul with every argument to make it follow me in striving after You. It held back with no excuse left, only a silent shrinking, fearing like death to be pulled from the habit that was killing it.

What light shines through me and strikes my heart without hurting it, so that I shudder and burn? I shudder because I am unlike it, burn because I am like it. It is Wisdom itself, breaking through my clouds, though the darkness my sins earn settles over me again.

I too ask, my God, where You are. In You I breathe a little when I pour out praise, then sink back into sadness. My faith says: hope in the Lord and endure the night of the wicked and his wrath, still bearing sin in us, until day breaks.
No one should seek their own good; each should seek their neighbour's good.

Be united, compassionate, loving and kind; don't repay evil or insult in kind, but bless, since you were called to inherit a blessing. Whoever wants a good life must guard their tongue, turn from evil, do good and pursue peace; the Lord watches over the righteous but opposes evildoers.

A man is all alone, with no son or brother, yet his work never ends and his wealth never satisfies him. He asks whom he is toiling for, depriving himself of joy. This too is meaningless, a miserable business.

Yahweh passed by and proclaimed himself merciful and gracious, slow to anger, rich in loving kindness and truth, forgiving sin for thousands; yet he will not clear the guilty, but brings the parents' sins upon their children and grandchildren to the third and fourth generation.
Strengthen weak hands and shaky knees. Tell the fearful: be strong, don't be afraid; your God is coming with vengeance and retribution, and he will come and save you.

The Lord's Spirit is on me: Yahweh anointed me to bring good news to the humble, heal the broken-hearted, free captives, proclaim his year of favour and our God's day of vengeance, and comfort mourners, giving joy for ashes, so they become his righteous planting, for his glory.

The wise show it by gentle good conduct. If bitter jealousy and selfish ambition fill your heart, don't boast or lie against the truth: that wisdom is earthly, sensual and demonic, breeding disorder and evil. Wisdom from above is pure, peaceful, gentle, merciful and sincere, and peacemakers sow righteousness.

Your fights and wars come from the cravings battling inside you. You want and don't get, so you murder and covet, and fight. You don't have because you don't ask; and when you ask, you don't receive, because you want it only for your pleasures.

Yahweh says: cursed is whoever trusts in people and turns from him; he will be like a desert shrub in parched salt land. Blessed is whoever trusts in Yahweh; he will be like a tree by water, green in heat, unworried in drought, always bearing fruit.

Blessed are the poor in spirit and those persecuted for righteousness, for heaven is theirs; mourners will be comforted, the gentle inherit the earth, those hungry for righteousness be filled, the merciful receive mercy, the pure in heart see God, and peacemakers be called God's children.

Have mercy on me, Yahweh, for I am in distress. Grief and sorrow waste my eyes, soul, body and years; my own sin has drained my strength. My enemies have made me despised; neighbours and friends flee me, and I am forgotten like the dead, like broken pottery.

My heart was bitter and I was senseless as a beast before you. Yet I am always with you; you hold my hand, guide me, and will afterwards receive me into glory. I desire no one but you; though body and heart fail, God is my strength and portion forever.

Yahweh is merciful, gracious and slow to anger; he won't accuse forever or repay us for our sins. His love for those who fear him is as high as the heavens; he removes our sins as far as east from west, pitying them like a father, knowing we are dust.

Sailors on the great waters see Yahweh's wonders: he commands the storm that tosses them until they reel and lose courage. Then they cry to Yahweh, and he rescues them, calms the storm, and brings them gladly to the harbour they longed for.

Don't repay evil for evil; live at peace with everyone as far as you can. Don't take revenge, but leave room for God's wrath, for vengeance is his. Feed your hungry enemy and give him drink; that will heap burning coals on his head. Overcome evil with good.
Watch for the right moment and beware of evil, and don't be ashamed about your own soul. For there is a shame that leads to sin, and a shame that brings honour and grace.

People have no fixed limits. Everyone feels not fully understood, and if there is truth in him and he rests finally on the divine soul, that must be so: some inner room is never opened. So everyone believes he has greater possibilities.

While we keep company with what is above us, we grow younger, not older. The young look up and learn from everything, but at seventy people think they know all and lose hope. Let them become vessels of the Holy Spirit, love and see truth, and hope and power return.

In nature every moment is new; only what is coming is sacred, and nothing is secure but life and change. No oath protects a love from a higher love, nor any truth from new thought. People want to be settled, but only being unsettled gives them hope.

Be patient; we will win in the end. Daily chores are soon forgotten, but in solitude a person finds sanity and insight that last. Ignore ridicule and defeat and rise again: justice will yet win, and the world exists to turn genius into practical power.

Trust yourself. Accept the place divine providence has given you, as great men did, sensing that what is fully trustworthy works within them. We must accept that same high destiny, not as cowards or invalids but as guides, redeemers and benefactors, obeying the Almighty and advancing on chaos.

Our craving to know the future confesses sin, and God gives no answer. The veil over tomorrow comes not from God's decree but from human nature: the soul lets us read only cause and effect, teaching us to live today. Drop idle curiosity, work and live, and the answer comes.

We are upset not by events but by our opinions about them; death isn't terrible, or Socrates would have thought so. So when troubled, blame our own opinions, not others. The untaught blame others, the beginner blames himself, and the fully taught blames neither.
How strange that you pity the slow of foot but not the slow of mind, and the blind in eye rather than the blind in heart.

We all climb toward our heart's desire. If another climber steals your sack and purse and grows fat and loaded, pity him: his climb will be harder and longer. And if, lean as you are, you see him heaving himself upward, help him a step; it will speed you.

If you are too weak to fix yourself on Me always, don't despair: worship Me steadily; if not, work for Me; if even that fails, take refuge in Me and give up the fruits of your work. Worship beats knowledge, renunciation beats both, and peace lies very near renunciation.

Better your own duty done imperfectly than another's done well. Whoever does his nature-given task does not sin; don't abandon it, Prince, though it bears blame, for all work has fault as fire has smoke. Only one working with free mind, subdued soul, dead desires and renounced results is released.

Wisdom means not acting hastily, not clinging to your opinions, and not believing or repeating all you hear. Seek advice from a wise, conscientious person and learn from your betters. A good life makes one wise before God; the humbler and more obedient to God, the wiser and more peaceful.

Trusting in people or created things is futile. Don't be ashamed to serve others for Christ's love or to seem poor. Hope in God, not yourself: do what you can and God will help. Trust not learning or cleverness but God's favour; he resists the proud and helps the humble.

Breaking a habit is hard, opposing your own will harder. But if you can't overcome small obstacles, how will you overcome great ones? Resist your will early and unlearn bad habits before they lead to worse. If you knew the peace and joy holy living brings, you'd be more zealous.

Long talk with people often leaves us less than we were; silence is easier than measured speech. So whoever seeks the spiritual must go apart from the crowd with Jesus. Only one who loves staying home goes out safely, who loves silence speaks safely, who loves obeying commands safely.

Some keep peace within and with others; some have none and give none, troubling others but themselves most. Yet all our peace here lies in humble suffering, not in escaping hardship. Whoever suffers best has most peace: master of himself, lord of the world, Christ's friend and heir of heaven.

If you were pure inside, you would see everything rightly and unharmed. A pure heart sees into heaven and hell; we judge outwardly as we are inwardly. The pure have joy; the bad conscience knows anguish best. As fire cleans rusty iron, turning wholly to God makes a person new.

A pure conscience brings peace. Praise doesn't make you holier nor blame worse; you are what God judges you to be. People see deeds, God sees intent. A humble spirit always does well and thinks little of itself; seeking no comfort from created things shows great purity and faithfulness.

Blessed is whoever knows what it is to love Jesus and despise himself for his sake, giving up all he loves, for Jesus must be loved above all. Love of created things fails; his lasts. He won't abandon you when all leave you, as one day they must.

At times God will forsake you, others will try you and you will weary yourself; you must bear it as long as God wills and be humbled. Only sufferers truly grasp Christ's Passion. The Cross awaits everywhere, for you carry yourself; patience brings inner peace and the everlasting crown.

Love is swift, sincere, gentle, strong, patient, faithful and never selfish; seeking your own is falling from love. It is humble, steady, chaste, obedient to authority, lowly in its own eyes, grateful to God and trusting him even when he hides his face, for love cannot live without sorrow.

Lord, Your care for me exceeds any I can give myself. As long as my will stays firm in You, do with me what You will, for it can only be good. Blessed be You whether You leave me in darkness or light, comfort me or cause me trouble.

Whoever has fewer gifts shouldn't be downcast or envious, but look to You and praise Your goodness, for You give freely to all. Everything comes from You, so You are praised in all. Why one has less and another more is Yours to know, for You know what each deserves.

Do you expect spiritual comfort at will? My saints had grief and desolation instead, yet bore it patiently, trusting God, knowing present suffering is nothing beside the coming glory. Wait for the Lord, be strong, devote yourself to God's glory; I will reward you richly and stand by you.

What do You ask of a guilty sinner above all, but sorrow and humility for his sins? True contrition brings hope of pardon, a reconciled conscience, recovered grace and escape from the wrath to come, as God and the penitent soul hurry to meet with a holy kiss.

Lord, my trust and comfort is You, whose mercies are endless. When was I well without You, or harmed with You near? I'd rather be poor or a pilgrim with You than rich, or in heaven, without You. Where You are is heaven; where You aren't, death and hell.

Each morning tell yourself: today I'll meet meddling, ungrateful, arrogant, deceitful, envious people, ignorant of good and evil. But the wrongdoer is my kin, sharing reason and the divine, so he cannot harm me nor I hate him. We are made to cooperate; resenting or turning away is against nature.

Remember how long you have delayed and how many chances the gods gave you. See what universe you belong to and what governor your life flows from; your time is fixed, and unless you use it to clear your mind, it will go, and you too, never to return.

Do each present task with simple dignity, kindness, freedom and justice, setting aside other thoughts. You will, if you do each act as your last, free of carelessness, hypocrisy, self-love and discontent. Hold these few things and you live a quiet life like the gods', who ask nothing more.

People seek retreats in the country, by the sea or in the mountains, but you can retreat into yourself anytime, and nowhere is quieter or freer than your own soul. Tranquillity is a well-ordered mind. Retreat there often, keeping brief basic principles that cleanse you and send you back content.

Am I capable of this? If so, I use my mind as a tool given by nature. If not, I step aside for someone better, unless there's reason not to, or do my best with a helper. Whatever I do, alone or with others, should serve the common good.

When troubled, you have forgotten: all happens by universal nature; another's wrong is nothing to you; all things always happen so; humans are kin through mind; each mind is divine; child, body and soul come from the deity; all is opinion; and you live and lose only the present.

Your children are not your own; they are Life longing for itself, coming through you, not from you. Give them love, not your thoughts; house their bodies, not their souls, which live in a tomorrow you can't visit. Strive to be like them, not to make them like you.

Happiness is lowly, not greedy, so it never gluts desire. What you think lofty seems small to those who reach it, and they climb higher. Ignorant of truth and led by common talk, people chase things as good, then find them bad, empty or lesser. Crowds mistake big for good.

If you learn little and lack ethics, you're criticised for both; learn little but are ethical, you're praised for ethics; learn much but lack ethics, you're criticised for ethics, as your learning failed; learn much and are ethical, you're praised for both.

Mendicants, fully cultivating the heart's release by love brings eleven benefits: easy sleep, happy waking, no bad dreams, love of humans and non-humans, protection by deities, safety from fire, poison and blade, quick immersion, a bright face, dying unconfused, and, if you go no higher, rebirth in a divine realm.
Just as a fragrant, lovely lotus can bloom from a heap of roadside trash, so a disciple of the Buddha, among those thought worthless, outshines blind ordinary people with wisdom.

Friends can't help when you die; heirs take your wealth, and beings fare on by their deeds. Riches, family and kingdom don't follow you, nor buy long life or stop old age. Life is short for all; the fool lies stricken by his own folly, but the wise don't tremble.

Don't run back to the past or anticipate the future; see clearly what is present, and know and foster the unshakable. Work keenly today, for death may come tomorrow and won't bargain. One who meditates tirelessly like this, night and day, has had one fine night, says the peaceful sage.

A thirsty, exhausted man is offered a delicious-looking drink but told it is poisoned and will bring death or deadly pain, so he quenches his thirst another way. In the same way, past ascetics saw pleasant things as impermanent, suffering, not-self, diseased and dangerous, and gave up craving.

Asked what a parrot tree is like, different people describe it as blackish, reddish, flaking or leafy, each rightly for the time they saw it. In the same way, those true persons each answered according to what they focused on when their vision was purified.
A tree leaning east, when cut at the root, falls east. In the same way, a mendicant who develops the noble eightfold path leans and inclines toward extinguishment.

The Buddha asks the sick Kassapa if his pain is easing; Kassapa says it is terrible and growing. The Buddha reminds him of the seven awakening factors he has rightly taught, which when developed lead to direct knowledge, awakening and extinguishment.

For one who lives for an idea or the good of all, pain matters less. Seen from goodness, pleasure may be shunned, pain sought, death welcomed, as martyrs show. As sea water weighs nothing when you dive in, on the moral plane pain lightens, giving near-superhuman patience under crushing persecution.

Better not to fill a vessel than carry it full. A point you keep fingering won't stay sharp. A hall full of gold and jade can't be kept safe. Wealth and honour turned to arrogance bring their own ruin. When work is done and fame grows, withdrawing is Heaven's way.

Favour and disgrace are both to be feared, and honour and great calamity are alike personal conditions. Disgrace means falling low after favour: gaining favour brings fear of losing it, and losing it brings fear of worse disaster. That is why favour and disgrace are equally feared.

I pictured the soul as a castle of diamond or clear crystal with many rooms, like heaven's many mansions. The soul of the just person is a paradise where God delights. Its beauty and powers are beyond our understanding, as God is, for he made us in his image.

We shouldn't be troubled by our thoughts: if from the devil, he leaves us alone when ignored; if frailties from Adam's sin, let us bear them patiently for love of God. Since we must eat and sleep, let us admit we are human and long for where none despise us.

Anxiously guarding feelings of devotion in prayer misunderstands union with God. The Lord wants works: care for a sick sister, feel her pain, fast so she may eat, because the Lord asks it. That is true union of wills. Rejoice when others are praised, and hide their faults.

Tears are not enough; what matters is hard work and virtue, letting tears come when God sends them, for they water the soul as no digging can. So we should stand before God, weigh His mercy and our vileness, and accept water or drought; then we have peace.

The only cure for bad habits is good counter-habits. Keep doing good and thinking holy thoughts to suppress bad impressions. Never call anyone hopeless: a person's character is a bundle of habits that new, better ones can check. Character is repeated habit, and only repeated habit can reform it.

Nachiketas told Death: these pleasures last a day and wear out the senses, and even the longest life is short. Keep your horses, chariots, dances and songs. Wealth cannot satisfy a person, nor can we keep it when we face you; we live only as long as you wish.

Pull away from the world's petty selfish clingings and don't make humanity the centre of your interests. Stand apart as a witness and student, unattached to people, and watch love work itself out. Frictions and falls are passing; outside the world's current you see God showing Himself as Love everywhere.

As the Bible says, if you can't love the brother you see, how can you love the unseen God? If you can't see God in a human face, you won't find him in clouds, images or stories. Seeing God in people makes you religious, and explains turning the other cheek.

To gain liberation through work, work without desire or looking for results; such work brings knowledge, then freedom. Giving up work before you know brings misery. Work done for the Self doesn't bind. Neither seek pleasure nor fear pain from work; keep telling yourself mind and body work, not you.

Business is a harsh master: even when family die and your heart is breaking, you must keep working, and we think this right. This science demands more effort than any business ever could; many succeed in business, very few in this.

Crossing an Indian desert, I saw lovely lakes for a month; when one vanished as I approached, I realised all were mirages. Afterwards I still saw them but knew them as mirage, so they lost their power to deceive. So too the illusion of the universe will break one day.

You think differently as child, adult and old man; everyone changes. So your individuality is not in body, mind or thought. Beyond them is your Atman, and the Advaitist says this Atman is Brahman itself.

A wave differs from the ocean only by its form and name, which exist only with the wave; when it subsides, the same water remains. In the same way, Maya is what makes the difference between you and me, between animals and humans, and between gods and humans.

We can safely trust far more than we do, setting aside as much care for ourselves as we honestly give elsewhere. Nature fits our weakness as well as our strength. Constant anxiety and strain is an almost incurable disease.

I went to the woods to live deliberately, facing only life's essentials, to learn what it could teach and not find at death that I had never lived. I didn't want to live what wasn't life, life being so precious, nor to resign myself unless truly necessary.

Whoever follows the faint, steady promptings of his genius may not see what extremes, even madness, they lead to, yet his road lies there. No one was ever misled by his genius; even bodily weakness wouldn't be regretted. If you greet each day and night with joy, that is success.

If we knew all of Nature's laws, one fact would reveal everything. We know few, so our results fail through our ignorance, not Nature's disorder. Unseen concurring laws make a harmony more wonderful still. Laws are like viewpoints on a mountain: endless profiles, but one true form, never grasped whole.

Advance confidently toward your dreams and live the life you imagined, and you'll meet unexpected success, and freer laws will form around you. The more you simplify, the simpler the universe seems; solitude, poverty and weakness cease to be such. Build castles in the air, then put foundations under them.

An artist of Kouroo resolved to make a perfect staff, believing time does not enter perfect work. He searched for the right wood while his friends grew old and died, but he did not age; his singleness of purpose and piety kept him young, and Time could not overcome him.

When an acorn and a chestnut fall side by side, neither holds back for the other; each grows by its own laws until one perhaps overshadows and destroys the other. A plant that cannot live by its nature dies, and so does a man.
